title: Polynomial translation modules are acyclic for internal lattice invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. Let $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$ and put $A(S)=C(S,F)$ on the coherent profinite site, using all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For integers $r,m\geq0$ put $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology. Let $T_{r,m}$ be the internal direct sum of copies of $A$ on the monomials in $r+m$ variables $y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_m$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give it the internal $A$-linear $L$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] determined by
$$(g\cdot f)(y,z)=f(y-g,z).$$
For a varying $g\in C(S,L)$ its coordinates are sections of $A(S)$ by $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F$; the formula is polynomial substitution and extends to the internal direct sum. Work with ordinary internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and ordinary total right derived invariants [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] in compatible coefficient universes containing all profinite parameter sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Then
$$R^q\Gamma_{A,L}(T_{r,m})=0\qquad(q>0)$$
as internal $A$-modules, where $R^q\Gamma$ is the $q$th cohomology object of $R\Gamma(T_{r,m}[0])$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This includes $r=0$ and $m=0$. The module is the polynomial direct sum, without a degree bound, and $A_\Omega$ retains its noncomplete norm topology.

proof.text: Prove the assertion by induction on $r$, simultaneously for every $m\geq0$. If $r=0$, $L=1$ and the identity axiom forces every action to be trivial, so fixed sections and their inclusion are the identity functor and identity map. Its derived functor is again the identity; a module in degree zero has zero positive cohomology. This proves the base case for all polynomial spectator modules, including $m=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of polynomial translation acyclicity, rank-zero base case

proof.text: Assume $r>0$ and the assertion for $r-1$, simultaneously for every spectator count. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ on $y_1$, $G=\mathbf Z_\ell^{r-1}$ on the other $y$ variables, and reorder $L=G\times H$. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-rank-one-difference-model], the polynomial stages $V_n$ of total degree at most $n$ with $D_n=-\partial/\partial y_1$ and $e_n=n+1$ form a finite ind-unipotent system, the colimit of $M_n(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V_n)$ in internal action modules is equivariantly $T_{r,m}$, and $\exp(D)-1=\Delta$ with $\Delta f=f(y_1-1,y_2,\ldots,z)-f(y_1,y_2,\ldots,z)$. These are the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-ind-unipotent-procyclic-difference] for the profinite group $G$ and either $F$. Transporting along the equivariant isomorphism, it gives $R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])\cong Q[T_{r,m}\xrightarrow{\Delta}T_{r,m}]$ in $D(\mathcal A_G(A))$, with degree-zero identification by the common inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: rank-one reduction, old steps 2-3

proof.text: Put $B=A[y_2,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_m]$. Regrouping the monomial coproduct by the exponent of $y_1$ identifies $T_{r,m}=B[y_1]$. The $G$-action is by $A$-algebra automorphisms on $B$ and fixes $y_1$. The coefficient ring contains the rational constants. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-difference-deformation-retract] with $d=r-1+m$: its derived isomorphism identifies $Q[T_{r,m}\xrightarrow{\Delta}T_{r,m}]$ with $B[0]$. Thus $R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])\cong B[0]$ as a derived $G$-action module.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: explicit difference contraction, old step 4

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], $\mathcal A_1(A),\mathcal A_G(A),\mathcal A_{G\times H}(A)$ are Grothendieck abelian. Take $L_a$ to be trivial inflation to $G$, $L_b$ projection inflation to $G\times H$, and $L_c$ total inflation. They are exact additive left adjoints with right adjoints $\Gamma_G,\Gamma_H^G,\Gamma_{G\times H}$. The identity $L_bL_a=L_c$ has conjugate $\Gamma_{G\times H}=\Gamma_G\Gamma_H^G$: after every profinite base change, a section is product-fixed exactly when it is fixed by both factors, since $(g,h)=(g,1)(1,h)$. Both adjunction transposes restrict the same map along the same invariant inclusion. Use the derived adjunctions induced by these specified underived adjunctions. Thus [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] applies to these specified adjunctions and gives
$$R\Gamma_{G\times H}(T_{r,m}[0])\cong R\Gamma_G R\Gamma_H^G(T_{r,m}[0])\cong R\Gamma_G(B[0]).$$
The $G$-module $B$ is $T_{r-1,m}$ by relabelling the remaining $y$ coordinates. The induction hypothesis kills its positive cohomology. This proves every rank and spectator count over either $F$, retaining the stated coefficient topology.
